threat_model: No threat model under docs/security/threat-models covers this front-end polish. None is needed: the diff adds no endpoint, no storage of user data and no new third-party origin. The relevant threats are reflected XSS through the query string, unsafe links in untrusted LLM output, PII leaking to analytics, URLs or storage, and the lead request shape drifting from the backend contract. Each is checked below.

findings.summary: FF-8 stores more than positions. The sessionStorage key is `${location.key}|${pathname}${search}${hash}`, so every visited URL's full query string and fragment is kept in sessionStorage['sarayatech:scroll-positions'] for the life of the tab (up to 50 entries, saved on pagehide). The browser probe confirmed it: hostile query strings were stored verbatim. The values are only JSON-parsed into a Map and compared as keys, never rendered or sent, so there is no injection. The site itself never puts PII in a URL: forms POST JSON, and FF-10 values are allow-listed. The residual risk is data minimisation only. An inbound link carrying PII in its query (an email-campaign ?email=, a third-party ?name=) would be copied into storage. That storage is readable by any same-origin script, though such a script could read location and history anyway. The comment at line 11 says 'positions are kept per history entry', which understates what is kept.
findings.fix: Key the map by `${location.key}|${location.pathname}` only, without search or hash. Location.key is already unique per history entry, and the 'default' key on a first load then shares one slot per path, which is acceptable. Or hash the search part before storing it. Add a ScrollToTop test asserting that sessionStorage never contains a query value such as '?email=a@b.c'. Non-blocking.

backend_follow_ups: None blocking. Confirmed that wt-be-next lib/validation.ts:165-210 caps chat history at 10 items, 2000 chars each and 15000 chars in total. The client's maximum (5 x 1000 user + 5 x 2000 assistant) is exactly 15000, so raising CHAT_LIMITS.message on either side without the other turns every long conversation into a 400 and a silent local fallback. Keep the two constants pinned by a contract test.

Informational, pre-existing: history 'assistant' turns are asserted by the client, so a visitor can forge prior assistant content to prime the model. The backend must keep treating history as untrusted. It must never use history to grant tools or data, and its system prompt must not rely on prior assistant turns being genuine.
not_verified: The backend was read for the history caps only, not reviewed.
verdict_rationale: Every sensitive area in the brief was checked against code, executed tests, probes and a real browser. The lead request shape and honeypot are unchanged against the contract. The FF-10 allow-list is exact and reflects nothing. Chat links are allow-listed with every probed obfuscation refused, there is no raw HTML or images, the request is {message, history} with no credentials, and abort leaks no state. The retired components are unreachable, and their guard bites on static and dynamic imports. The only finding is low and non-blocking, so no Critical or High remains. PASS against bde572b.
